impact: Live repro: provider=codex on gpt-5.5 returned `UNKNOWN_ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. ... try again at Jul 28th`. classifyCodexError (src/backends/codex.ts ~line 67) only matches '429' / 'rate_limit' / 'rate limit', so the ChatGPT-tier "usage limit" / "hit your usage limit" wording falls through to UNKNOWN_ERROR. Two harms: (1) the user gets a vague UNKNOWN_ERROR instead of an actionable rate/quota error; (2) it blocks reliable provider failover, which must key on an accurate out-of-usage classification. Fix: add "usage limit" / "hit your usage limit" (and "quota") to the RATE_LIMITED branch. Prerequisite for the failover feature.
resolution: Fixed in classifyError (src/backends/codex.ts): the rate-limit branch now also matches "usage limit" / "hit your usage limit" / "quota", so a hit ChatGPT-tier usage cap classifies as RATE_LIMITED instead of UNKNOWN_ERROR. Verified live (real out-of-usage Codex now classifies as RATE_LIMITED and triggers failover). Commit 09fa68e; covered by codex.test.ts "returns RATE_LIMITED for usage-limit / quota wording (ISS-008)".
title: Codex "usage limit" error misclassified as UNKNOWN_ERROR (should be RATE_LIMITED)
